justification: Version 4 changes one rule of version 3 (budget-policy.v3.json, SHA-256 bc9c1d063b4f9d5cac17b851a5ea547638bb4feeab796a9a7292a99e92c9d7c5): the memory-rule floor of three peak-RSS cells rises from 1.1 to 1.15 (thresholdRule.memoryFloor): synthetic-c1000-t200-r20-s307 session.maxRssBytes (median), synthetic-c10000-t1000-r100-s307 session.maxRssBytes (min), synthetic-c10000-t1000-r100-s307 full.maxRssBytes (min). Their statistics are unchanged. Cause: after CE-02.1 and AG-01.1, these cells sit at their version 3 limits. c10000 session.maxRssBytes (minimum) measured about 1,345 MB against a limit of 1,347.6 MB, and one gate failed it by 0.16 MB; c1000 session.maxRssBytes (median) measured about 382-386 MB against 393.3 MB; c10000 full.maxRssBytes (minimum) is at about +8-9%. Cumulative core-evolution growth of session peak RSS is about +9.8% over alpha1 against the 10% budget. Recovery was attempted first: #130 recovered what was recoverable; the CE-02.1 investigation found nothing to recover (CE-02.1 retains about 0.4 MB); #150 (a private Babel copy) traded c10000 against c1000 and was closed. The remaining growth is the legitimate cost of the planned capabilities. The c1000 high mode stays visible: the c1000 cell keeps the median, because its high mode is a real effect of the candidates (alpha1 never reaches it on the measurement host), not measurement noise. The floor is cumulative against alpha1 for the whole epic, like the timing floor: the remaining headroom on these cells is about 5% and later lots must not assume more. CE-12.3 (#76) owns the final performance qualification and the recovery of this cost. Every other rule is unchanged: the 1.25 timing floor, the runtime floor, the memory floor (1.1) of every other memory budget, the memory rule, the statistics, deterministic growth, identity, metrics, workloads, noise ceiling, minimum pairs and rounding. As the change policy requires, every budget is re-derived from a new comparable baseline of the unchanged alpha1 artifact on the measurement host (alpha1-v4-sk-d1 and alpha1-v4-sk-d2, the first two admissible attempts of the pre-registered series D); the version 3 evidence is not reused. Every budget whose derived limit loosens relative to version 3 is listed in relaxations, generated from the derivation. The absolute limits remain bound to the measurement host.

comparison: Run tools/baselines/measure.mjs with the final plan and both --epoch alpha1=<alpha1 closure> and --epoch <candidate>=<candidate closure> on one machine (--require-quiet is optional). budgets.mjs gate pairs each candidate sample with the adjacent alpha1 sample of the same round, applies the paired-ratio, absolute-memory, deterministic and identity budgets, requires alpha1 to reproduce its frozen deterministic outputs, and lists unknown metrics. Verdicts: pass only when every budget passes; fail on any failing budget, workload-record mismatch, altered alpha1 tarball or policy-chain problem; inconclusive when the run lacks the interleaved control, has too few pairs, exceeds a noise ceiling or cannot resolve a limit; incomplete when a budgeted metric was not run.

changePolicy: budgets.v4.json is generated by `node tools/baselines/budgets.mjs freeze` from this policy and the committed baseline results, and is never edited by hand; rerunning the same freeze command with this policy and the referenced results must reproduce it byte for byte.

Committed policy, budgets, workloads, derivation and baseline result files are immutable; `budgets.mjs gate` compares the budgets file with the version of the commit that added it and fails on any difference.

Changing a threshold, metric set or workload requires a new budget-policy.vN.json and budgets.vN.json (N incremented), a justification, a predecessor reference by path and SHA-256, and a new comparable baseline run of the unchanged alpha1 artifact; reusing an old result file is rejected.
Every budget loosened or removed relative to the predecessor must be listed in `relaxations` with its own justification; an unknown metric may only leave the unknown list by gaining a budget.

No release may pass against a weakened budget retroactively: the gate evaluates the budgets version current at the evaluated commit, fails on any policy-chain problem, and never reports inconclusive or incomplete as pass.
